agent.name: NCERT Document Sketch Agent
agent.prompt_template:
You are helping build a retrieval index for NCERT PDFs.

Given the chapter/document text and a small header, produce a compact JSON "document sketch" that can be reused
for contextualizing many chunks from the same document.

Header:
{{ header }}

Document (may be truncated):
{{ document_text }}

Return a single JSON object with these keys:
- chapter_title: best-effort title (empty string if unknown)
- main_sections: array of short section headings (best-effort)
- key_definitions: object mapping term -> short definition (keep very short; include only important terms)
- concepts: array of important terms/entities a student might search for (10–30 items)

Rules:
- Output JSON only. No markdown fences. No extra keys.
- Keep it compact: do not quote long excerpts.

inputs.header: NCERT Class 12 Physics Ch.3 Current Electricity
inputs.document_text: 3.1 Introduction. Electric current is the flow of electric charge through a conductor. 3.2 Electric Current. The current I = dQ/dt; drift velocity and mobility relate microscopic motion to macroscopic current. Ohm's law: V = IR for ohmic conductors at constant temperature. 3.3 Ohm's Law and Resistance. Resistivity ρ = RA/L; temperature dependence of resistance. 3.4 Electrical Energy and Power. P = VI = I²R; heating effect Joule's law. 3.5 Cells in Series and Parallel. EMF, internal resistance, terminal voltage. 3.6 Kirchhoff's Rules. Junction rule ΣI_in = ΣI_out; loop rule ΣΔV = 0. Example 3.1: Finding current in a series circuit. Example 3.2: Wheatstone bridge balance. Exercise 3.1–3.15 on combination of resistors and meter bridge. ncert-1

key_definitions.Ohm's Law: V = IR; relationship between voltage, current, and resistance.
key_definitions.Resistivity: ρ = RA/L; material property affecting resistance.
key_definitions.Electrical Power: P = VI = I²R; rate of energy transfer.
key_definitions.EMF: Electromotive force; voltage provided by a source.
key_definitions.Internal Resistance: Resistance within a cell affecting output voltage.
key_definitions.Joule's Law: Heating effect of current in a resistor.
key_definitions.Kirchhoff's Loop Rule: ΣΔV = 0; conservation of energy in circuits.

inputs.header: NCERT Class 11 Biology Ch.16 Digestion and Absorption
inputs.document_text: 16.1 Digestive System. Alimentary canal and associated glands. 16.2 Digestion of Food. Carbohydrates: salivary amylase in mouth; pancreatic amylase. Proteins: pepsin in stomach (HCl activates pepsinogen); trypsin in duodenum. Fats: bile emulsification; lipase action. 16.3 Absorption. Villi and microvilli increase surface area; absorption in small intestine. Table 16.1: Enzymes, site of action, and products. Activity 16.1: Testing action of salivary amylase on starch. Exercise questions on disorders of digestion and enzyme specificity. ncert-2

key_definitions.Alimentary canal: The whole passage along which food passes through the body.
key_definitions.Salivary amylase: Enzyme that breaks down carbohydrates in the mouth.
key_definitions.Pepsin: Enzyme that digests proteins in the stomach.
key_definitions.Trypsin: Enzyme that continues protein digestion in the duodenum.
key_definitions.Villi: Small finger-like projections in the small intestine that absorb nutrients.
key_definitions.Microvilli: Tiny projections on villi that increase surface area for absorption.

inputs.header: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Ch.4 Chemical Bonding
inputs.document_text: 4.1 Kossel-Lewis approach. Octet rule and limitations. 4.2 Ionic Bonding. Lattice enthalpy; Born-Haber cycle. 4.3 Covalent Bonding. VSEPR theory predicts geometry from electron pair repulsion. 4.4 Valence Bond Theory. Hybridisation sp, sp², sp³; sigma and pi bonds. 4.5 Molecular Orbital Theory. Bond order; paramagnetic vs diamagnetic. Example 4.1: NH₃ pyramidal geometry. Example 4.2: O₂ MO configuration. Exercise 4.1–4.12 on polarity, dipole moment, and hydrogen bonding. ncert-3

key_definitions.Octet Rule: Atoms tend to form bonds to achieve a full outer shell of eight electrons.
key_definitions.Ionic Bonding: Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.
key_definitions.Lattice Enthalpy: Energy required to separate one mole of an ionic solid into gaseous ions.
key_definitions.Covalent Bonding: Sharing of electron pairs between atoms.
key_definitions.VSEPR Theory: Predicts molecular geometry based on electron pair repulsion.
key_definitions.Hybridisation: Mixing of atomic orbitals to form new hybrid orbitals.
key_definitions.Sigma Bond: Single covalent bond formed by head-on overlap of orbitals.
key_definitions.Pi Bond: Bond formed by the side-to-side overlap of p orbitals.
key_definitions.Bond Order: Number of bonds between two atoms.
key_definitions.Paramagnetic: Substances with unpaired electrons that are attracted to magnetic fields.
key_definitions.Diamagnetic: Substances with all electrons paired that are repelled by magnetic fields.

inputs.document_text: 7.1 Integration as inverse of differentiation. Indefinite integral ∫f(x)dx = F(x) + C. 7.2 Methods: substitution, partial fractions, integration by parts. 7.3 Definite integrals. Fundamental theorem: ∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx = F(b) − F(a). 7.4 Area under a curve between x = a and x = b. Example 7.1: ∫ x√(1−x²) dx by substitution. Example 7.2: Area bounded by parabola. Theorem 7.1: Properties of definite integrals. Exercise 7.1–7.20. ncert-4

key_definitions.Definite integral: Integral with limits, ∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx = F(b) − F(a).
key_definitions.Substitution: Method to simplify integrals by changing variables.
key_definitions.Partial fractions: Method to break down rational functions for integration.
key_definitions.Integration by parts: Method based on the product rule of differentiation.
key_definitions.Area under a curve: The definite integral represents the area between the curve and the x-axis.

inputs.document_text: 7.1 Equilibrium in physical processes. Solid-liquid, liquid-vapour equilibrium. 7.2 Chemical equilibrium. Kc = [products]/[reactants]; homogeneous and heterogeneous. 7.3 Le Chatelier's principle. Effect of concentration, pressure, temperature. 7.4 Ionic equilibrium. Ka, Kb, Kw; pH scale; buffer solutions. Example 7.1: Calculating Kc from equilibrium concentrations. Exercise 7.1–7.18 on Q vs K and degree of dissociation. ncert-7

key_definitions.Le Chatelier's principle: System adjusts to counteract changes in equilibrium.

inputs.document_text: 12.1 Electric current and circuit. Ammeter, voltmeter, switch. 12.2 Ohm's law V = IR. Resistance R = ρL/A. 12.3 Factors affecting resistance. Series: R = R₁+R₂; parallel: 1/R = 1/R₁+1/R₂. 12.4 Heating effect. H = I²Rt; electric fuse. 12.5 Electric power P = VI. Commercial unit kWh. Activity 12.1: Compare current in series vs parallel. Exercise 12.1–12.10. ncert-8

key_definitions.Ohm's law: V = IR, relationship between voltage, current, and resistance.
key_definitions.Electric power: Rate of doing work, P = VI.

inputs.header: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics Ch.4 Quadratic Equations
inputs.document_text: 4.1 Standard form ax²+bx+c=0. Roots by factorisation and quadratic formula. 4.2 Discriminant D = b²−4ac determines nature of roots. 4.3 Sum and product of roots: −b/a and c/a. 4.4 Word problems on area, speed, and consecutive integers. Example 4.1: Finding roots when D > 0. Example 4.2: No real roots when D < 0. Exercise 4.1–4.4. ncert-9

key_definitions.Quadratic Equation: An equation of the form ax² + bx + c = 0.
key_definitions.Discriminant: D = b² - 4ac; determines the nature of roots.
key_definitions.Factorisation: Method to find roots by expressing the equation as a product.
key_definitions.Quadratic Formula: Roots can be found using x = (-b ± √D) / (2a).

inputs.document_text: 13.1 Photosynthesis as anabolic process. 6CO₂+6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆+6O₂. 13.2 Light reaction in grana: photolysis, ATP, NADPH. 13.3 Calvin cycle in stroma; RuBisCO; C3 pathway. 13.4 C4 pathway in maize and sugarcane; Kranz anatomy. Figure 13.4: Z-scheme of light reaction. Table 13.1: Cyclic vs non-cyclic photophosphorylation. Exercise 13.1–13.8. ncert-10

main_sections: C4 pathway in maize and sugarcane

key_definitions.Photosynthesis: Process by which plants convert light energy into chemical energy.
key_definitions.Photolysis: Splitting of water molecules during light reactions.
key_definitions.RuBisCO: Enzyme that catalyzes the first step of the Calvin cycle.
key_definitions.C3 pathway: Main pathway of carbon fixation in plants.
key_definitions.C4 pathway: Alternative pathway for carbon fixation in some plants.
key_definitions.Z-scheme: Model of electron transport in light reactions.
key_definitions.Photophosphorylation: Process of generating ATP using light energy.

inputs.header: NCERT Class 12 Physics Ch.9 Ray Optics
inputs.document_text: 9.1 Reflection; mirror formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. 9.2 Refraction; Snell's law n₁ sin i = n₂ sin r. 9.3 Total internal reflection; critical angle. 9.4 Lens formula 1/f = 1/v − 1/u; magnification m = v/u. 9.5 Prism deviation; dispersive power. Figure 9.12: Ray diagram for convex lens. Example 9.3: Image position. Exercise 9.1–9.15. ncert-11

key_definitions.Snell's Law: n₁ sin i = n₂ sin r
key_definitions.Dispersive Power: Ability of prism to separate colors

inputs.document_text: 3.1 Electrochemical cells. Anode oxidation; cathode reduction. 3.2 Standard electrode potential E°. Cell EMF E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode. 3.3 Nernst equation links EMF to concentration. 3.4 Conductance and molar conductivity; Kohlrausch law. 3.5 Batteries and fuel cells. Corrosion as electrochemical process. Example 3.1: Calculate Ecell at non-standard concentrations. Exercise 3.1–3.12. ncert-12

key_definitions.Standard electrode potential: Measure of the tendency of a chemical species to be reduced.
key_definitions.Conductance: Ability of a solution to conduct electricity.
key_definitions.Molar conductivity: Conductivity of a solution divided by its molarity.
key_definitions.Batteries: Devices that store chemical energy and convert it to electrical energy.
key_definitions.Fuel cells: Devices that convert chemical energy directly into electrical energy.

inputs.header: NCERT Class 12 Economics Ch.2 National Income
inputs.document_text: 2.1 Circular flow of income. Factor payments and expenditure. 2.2 GDP at market prices; GNP = GDP + NFIA. 2.3 NDP and NNP; depreciation. 2.4 Real vs nominal GDP; GDP deflator. 2.5 Methods of measuring national income: product, income, expenditure. Table 2.1: Relationship between macro aggregates. Exercise 2.1–2.8. ncert-13

key_definitions.Depreciation: Reduction in value of an asset

inputs.header: NCERT Class 10 Civics Ch.3 Gender Religion and Caste
inputs.document_text: 3.1 Gender and politics. Public/private division; women's political representation. 3.2 Religion communalism vs secularism in India. 3.3 Caste and politics. Reservation policy; caste-based mobilisation. Case study: Women's reservation bill debate. Exercise: Analyse how social divisions affect electoral outcomes. ncert-14

key_definitions.Communalism: Loyalty to a specific religious community.

inputs.header: NCERT Class 11 Mathematics Ch.7 Permutations and Combinations
inputs.document_text: 7.1 Fundamental principle of counting. Multiplication rule. 7.2 Permutations nPr = n!/(n−r)!. Circular permutations. 7.3 Combinations nCr = n!/[(n−r)!r!]. 7.4 Applications to binomial coefficients and probability. Example 7.1: Arrangements with repetition. Example 7.2: Selection problems. Exercise 7.1–7.10. ncert-15

main_sections: Applications to binomial coefficients and probability

key_definitions.Permutations: Arrangements of objects in a specific order.
key_definitions.Combinations: Selections of objects without regard to order.
key_definitions.nPr: Number of permutations of n items taken r at a time.
key_definitions.nCr: Number of combinations of n items taken r at a time.
key_definitions.Factorial: Product of all positive integers up to a given number.
